questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of internal diameter 18 cm contains water. This water is to be filled in cylindrical bottles of diameter 6 cm and height 3 cm. The number of bottles required to empty the bowl is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Hemispherical bowl of internal diameter 18 cm

Cylindrical bottles of diameter 6 cm and height 3 cm

**Concept Used:**

Volume of Hemisphere = (2)/(3)pir³

Volume of Cylinder = pi r² h

**Calculation:**

⇒ Radius of hemispherical bowl = (18)/(2) = 9

⇒ We know that, pi = (22)/(7)

⇒ Volume of water in hemispherical bowl = (2)/(3)pir3 = (2)/(3)pi × (9)³ = (2)/(3) × (22)/(7) × 9 × 9 × 9

⇒ Radius of cylindrical bottle = (6)/(2) = 3

⇒ Volume of 1 cylindrical bottle = pi r² h = (22)/(7) × (3)² × 3 = (22)/(7) × 3 × 3 × 3

⇒ Let number of required bottles = x

⇒ According to the question,

⇒ Volume of hemispherical bowl = Volume of 1 cylindrical bowl × Number of required bottles

⇒ (2)/(3) × (22)/(7) × 9 × 9 × 9 = (22)/(7) × 3 × 3 × 3 × x

⇒ (2)/(3) × 9 × 9 × 9 = 3 × 3 × 3 × x

⇒ (2)/(3) × 3 × 3 × 3 = x

⇒ x = 18

**Therefore, the number of bottles required to empty the bowl is 18.**

questions.question: The surface area of a sphere is 2464 cm². Find its volume.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Surface area of the sphere = 2464 cm².

**Formula Used:**

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr²

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³

**Calculation:**

Given surface area, 4πr² = 2464

⇒ r² = 2464 / 4π

⇒ r² = 2464 / (4 × 3.14)

⇒ r² = 2464 / 12.56

⇒ r² = 196

⇒ r = √196

⇒ r = 14 cm

Now, Volume = (4/3)πr³

⇒ Volume = (4/3)π(14)³

⇒ Volume = (4/3)π(2744)

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × 22/7 × 2744

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × 22 × 392

⇒ Volume ≈ 11498 (2)/(3) ~cm³

**The volume of the sphere is approximately **11498 (2)/(3) ~cm³**.**

questions.question: A solid hemisphere has radius 21 cm. It is melted to form a cylinder such that the ratio of its curved surface area to total surface area is 2 ∶ 5. What is the radius (in cm) of its base (take π = frac{{22}}{7})?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of a solid hemisphere is 21 cm.

The ratio of the cylinder's curved surface area to its Total surface area is 2/5.

**Formula used:**

The curved surface area of the cylinder = 2πRh

The total surface area of cylinder = 2πR(R + h)

The volume of the cylinder = πR²h

The volume of the solid hemisphere = 2/3πr³ 

(where r is the radius of a solid hemisphere and R is the radius of a cylinder)

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

CSA/TSA = 2/5

⇒ [2πRh]/[2πR(R + h)] = 2/5

⇒ h/(R + h) = 2/5

⇒ 5h = 2R + 2h

⇒ h = (2/3)R .......(1)

The cylinder's volume and the volume of a solid hemisphere are equal.

⇒ πR²h = (2/3)πr³

⇒ R2 × (2/3)R = (2/3) × (21)³

⇒ R³ = (21)3

⇒ R = 21 cm

**∴ The radius ****(in cm)**** of its base is 21 cm.**

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3. The length, breadth and height of the cuboid are increased by 200%, 300% and 300%, respectively. Then compared to the original volume, the increase in the volume of the cuboid will be :
questions.solution:
Given:

The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.

Formula used:

Volume of cuboid = Length(L) × Breadth(B) × Height(H)

Calculation:

Let the Length, breadth and height of the cuboid be 100, 200, and 300 respectively.

Volume of cuboid = 100 × 200 × 300 = 6000000

Length increased by 200%, Breadth increase by 300% and height by 300%

Now, new length = 300, breadth = 800 and height = 1200 respectively

⇒ new volume of cuboid = 300 × 800 × 1200

= 288000000

Increase in volume = (new volume of the cuboid – the volume of the cuboid)/volume of the cuboid

= (288000000 – 6000000)/6000000

= 282000000/6000000

= 47 times

**∴ The increase in the volume of the cuboid will be 47 times.**

Volume of a Cube

questions.question: The volume of a solid right circular cone is 600π cm³, and the diameter of its base is 30 cm. The total surface area (in cm²) of the cone is:

The volume of cone = 1over3πr²h

**Calculation:**

The volume of cone = 1over3πr2h

⇒ 1over3 × π × 15 × 15 × h = 600π

⇒​ h = (600 × 3)/(15 × 15)

⇒​ h = 8 cm

⇒​ l² = r² + h²

⇒​ l² = 15² + 8² = 225 + 64 = 289

⇒​ l = √289 = 17 cm

Total surface area = πr(r + l)

⇒​ π × 15 × (15 + 17)

⇒​ π × 15 × 32 = 480π cm².

questions.question:
A solid cone of radius 7 cm and height 7 cm was melted along with two solid spheres of radius 7 cm each to form a solid cylinder of radius 7 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm²) of the cylinder?

(Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **radius (r)** is same (7 cm) for all shapes, we can equate heights.

Volume of **Cylinder** = Volume of **Cone** + 2 × Volume of **Sphere**

πr²H = (1/3)πr²h + 2 × (4/3)πr³ ⇒ H = h/3 + 8r/3

H = 7/3 + (8 × 7)/3 = 63/3 = 21 cm

**CSA** = 2πrH = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 21 = 924 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 924 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Radius of cone, sphere, and cylinder (r) = 7 cm; Height of cone (h) = 7 cm.

**Formula Used:** Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²h; Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³; Volume of cylinder = πr²H; Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrH.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88a1f6c6e5ec84880e015c894dfe180525d55456fd4ed1626e73933c821b784f.png] 

⇒ Total Volume of melted items = (1/3) × π × 7² × 7 + 2 × (4/3) × π × 7³

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3)π(7³) + (8/3)π(7³) = (9/3)π(7³) = 3π(7³)

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = π × 7² × H

⇒ 3π × 7³ = π × 7² × H

⇒ H = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

⇒ Curved Surface Area of cylinder = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 21

⇒ CSA = 44 × 21 = 924 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 924 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved part and two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume Conservation

When a solid is melted and recast into another shape, its **Total Volume** remains constant.

Surface Area of Sphere

The surface area of a sphere is given by 4πr², which is four times the area of its great circle.</p

questions.question: The volumes of two cubes are in the ratio of 8 ∶ 27. If the volume of the larger cube is 513 cm³ more than that of the smaller cube, find the length of each side of the smaller cube.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Ratio of volume of two cubes is 8:27

Volume of the larger cube is 513 more than smaller cube

**FORMULA USED:**

Volume of a cube = a³ 

Where a = side of a cube 

**CALCULATION:**

Let us assume the volume of smaller cube be a³ 

Here, we have volume of ratio of cubes is 8 :27 

Let the volume of cubes of smaller and larger one be 8x and 27x respectively

Now, according to the given question,

Volume of larger cube = 513 + volume of smaller cube 

⇒ 27x = 513 + 8x 

⇒19x = 513 

⇒ x = 513/19 = 27 

Volume of smaller cube = 8x = 8 × 27 

But volume of smaller cube we have assumed is a³ .So, these two must be equal

⇒ a³ = 8 × 27 

⇒ a = 2 × 3 = 6 

**Hence, length of each side of the smaller cube is 6 cm.**

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 125%, then by what percentage will its surface area increase (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius increase = 125% ⇒ New radius = 1 + 1.25 = 2.25 times of original.

Surface Area depends on (radius)².

New Area = (2.25)² = 5.0625 times of original area.

Increase in Area = 5.0625 − 1 = 4.0625.

Percentage Increase = 4.0625 × 100 = 406.25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 406.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Increase in radius = 125%

Formula Used: Surface Area of Sphere = 4 × π × r²

 
 Old Area (A)
 
• 
 r
 
 New Area (5.0625A)
 
• 
 2.25r
 Radius Change: +125%

⇒ Let the initial radius be r₁ = 100 units.

⇒ Final radius r₂ = 100 + 125% of 100 = 225 units.

⇒ Initial Surface Area A₁ = 4 × π × (100)² = 40000π units².

⇒ Final Surface Area A₂ = 4 × π × (225)² = 4 × π × 50625 = 202500π units².

⇒ Increase in Area = 202500π − 40000π = 162500π units².

⇒ Percentage increase = (Increase in Area ÷ Initial Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (162500π ÷ 40000π) × 100 = 4.0625 × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 406.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 406.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Change of a Sphere

Since the volume of a sphere is proportional to r³, if the radius increases by x%, the volume increases by factor of (1 + x/100)³ − 1.

Successive Percentage Rule

For Area change (radius × radius), the net percentage change can be calculated using x + y + (xy/100). Here: 125 + 125 + (125 × 125 / 100) = 406.25%.

Surface Area vs. Diameter

Percentage change in radius, diameter, or circumference leads to the same percentage change in surface area because they are all linearly related.</p

questions.question: A solid metallic cube having surface area of 54 cm² is melted to form smaller cubes of surface area (8)/(12) cm2 each. Find the number of smaller cubes.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A solid metallic cube having surface area of 54 cm² is melted to form smaller cubes of surface area (8)/(12) cm² each.

**Formula used:**

Surface area of a cube = 6a² (where 'a' is the side length)

**Calculation:**

Let 'A' be the side length of the large cube.

6A² = 54

⇒ A² = 9

⇒ A = 3 cm

Volume of the large cube = A³ = 3³ = 27 cm³

Let 'a' be the side length of the smaller cubes.

Surface area of each smaller cube = 6a² = (8)/(12) cm²

⇒ a² = (8)/(12) / 6 = (8)/(72)

⇒ a² = (1)/(9)

⇒ a = 1/3 cm

Volume of each smaller cube = a³ = (1/3)³ = 1/27 cm³

Number of smaller cubes = Volume of large cube / Volume of one smaller cube

⇒ 27 / (1/27)

⇒ 27 × 27

⇒ 729

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: A solid metallic cube of side 6 sqrt[{3}]{4} cm, is melted and recast into a cuboid of length 12 cm and breadth 9 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the longest diagonal of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a solid is melted, Volume of Cube = Volume of Cuboid

⇒ (6 × ³√4)³ = 12 × 9 × h

⇒ 216 × 4 = 108 × h ⇒ h = 8 cm

Longest diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²) = √(12² + 9² + 8²)

⇒ Longest diagonal = √(144 + 81 + 64) = √289 = 17 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the cube (a) = 6 × ³√4 cm

Length of the cuboid (l) = 12 cm

Breadth of the cuboid (b) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cube = a³

Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h

Longest diagonal of a cuboid = √(l² + b² + h²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88709803b125899499f82a7816a8fc2ee8bc2c2786389592bbd1a914e2926a58.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the solid metallic cube is melted and recast into a cuboid, their volumes will be equal.

⇒ Volume of Cube = Volume of Cuboid

⇒ a³ = l × b × h

⇒ (6 × ³√4)³ = 12 × 9 × h

⇒ 6³ × (³√4)³ = 108 × h

⇒ 216 × 4 = 108 × h

⇒ 864 = 108 × h

⇒ h = 864 ÷ 108

⇒ h = 8 cm

Now, substitute the values of l, b, and h to find the length of the longest diagonal:

⇒ Longest diagonal = √(12² + 9² + 8²)

⇒ Longest diagonal = √(144 + 81 + 64)

⇒ Longest diagonal = √289

⇒ Longest diagonal = 17 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Melting and Recasting

When any 3D solid is melted to form a new solid, the total mass and volume remain perfectly conserved. (Volume of original solid = Volume of new solid)

Properties of a Cube

Volume = a³ | Total Surface Area = 6a² | Body Diagonal = a√3

Properties of a Cuboid

Volume = l × b × h | Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl) | Longest Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²)
</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 616 cm² and the area of its base is 38.5 cm². What is the volume (in cm³) of the cylinder? (Take pi = (22)/(7))

⇒ R2 = (77/2) × (7/22) = 49/4 .....(1)

∴ Height = 616 × (1/2) × (7/22) × (2/7) = 28 cm

Then, the volume = (22/7) × (49/4) × (28) = 1078 cm3

**∴ The volume (in cm3) of the cylinder is 1078 cm3**

questions.question: The cost of painting a spherical vessel of diameter 14 cm is Rs. 21,560. What is the cost of painting (in Rs.) per square centimetre? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate of painting = Total Cost ÷ Surface Area

Surface Area of **spherical vessel** = 4 × π × r²

Given: Diameter = 14 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 7 cm

Rate = 21,560 ÷ (4 × 22/7 × 7 × 7) = 21,560 ÷ 616 = 35

**∴ The correct answer is ₹35.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total cost of painting = ₹21,560

Diameter of the **spherical vessel** (d) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr²

Cost of painting = Surface Area × Rate per cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e9616b9fb695800401086f23ec018cd9a274be1dd997224d9595dab3b12e9ad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

⇒ Total Surface Area (TSA) = 4 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ TSA = 4 × 22 × 7

⇒ TSA = 88 × 7 = 616 cm²

⇒ Rate per cm² = Total Cost ÷ TSA

⇒ Rate = 21,560 ÷ 616

⇒ Rate = ₹35

**∴ The correct answer is ₹35.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3)πr³.

Surface Area of a Hemisphere

For a solid hemisphere, the **Curved Surface Area** is 2πr² and the **Total Surface Area** is 3πr².

Cost Calculation Rule

When painting or plating, cost is always calculated on the **outer boundary** (surface area), whereas for filling, **volume** is used.

questions.question: A right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is rotated about the sides of 3 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a right-angled triangle is rotated about one of its perpendicular sides, that side becomes the height of the generated cone.

Here, the triangle is rotated about the 3 cm side, so Height (h) = 3 cm.

The other perpendicular side becomes the base radius, so Radius (r) = 4 cm.

Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h = (1/3) × π × 4² × 3 = 16π cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 16π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of the right-angled triangle = 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm.

The triangle is rotated about the side of 3 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d30669837d996ed67a375642589bfd3d4b10359bbba7df20cd05fadac6a2a1b7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ When the triangle is rotated about the 3 cm side, this side becomes the axis of rotation.

⇒ Height of the cone (h) = 3 cm

⇒ Radius of the base (r) = 4 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = Hypotenuse = 5 cm

⇒ Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × (4)² × 3

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × 16 × 3

⇒ Volume = 16π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 16π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rotation about the other side

If the same right triangle was rotated about the 4 cm side instead, the height would be 4 cm and the radius would be 3 cm. The resulting volume would be (1/3) × π × 3² × 4 = 12π cm³.

Rotation about the hypotenuse

If the triangle is rotated about its hypotenuse (5 cm), it forms a double cone. The common radius of these cones is given by (Base × Perpendicular) ÷ Hypotenuse = (3 × 4) ÷ 5 = 2.4 cm.

Surface Areas of a Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl and Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(r + l), where r is the base radius and l is the slant height.
</p
